items.title: The Problem of Pattern and Scale in Ecology: The Robert H. MacArthur Award Lecture
items.summary: It is argued that the problem of pattern and scale is the central problem in ecology, unifying population biology and ecosystems science, and marrying basic and applied ecology. Applied challenges, such as the prediction of the ecological causes and consequences of global climate change, require the interfacing of phenomena that occur on very different scales of space, time, and ecological organization. items.summary: Brain-wide association studies have linked brain structure to complex mental health phenotypes, yet the genetic underpinnings of these effects remain largely unclear. Here, we leverage multimodal neuroimaging, behavioral and genetic data from the UK Biobank to develop an integrative framework combining brain-wide association studies and GWAS to elucidate how genetic variants affect the relationship between brain structure and mental health. items.summary: Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is a non-invasive neuromodulatory therapy gaining interest for its neural mechanisms and therapeutic effects. items.summary: Psychoanalysis occupies a unique position in psychiatry, simultaneously a body of knowledge, a method of clinical investigation, and a form of treatment. items.summary: Background Neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia and variable intellectual and behavioral abnormalities (NEDHIB) is a rare autosomal-dominant condition caused by pathogenic POLR2A variants. items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests
